articles.title: Social Security COLA for 2027: How to find out how much more you'll get
articles.summary: The Social Security COLA will increase by 3.6% in 2027, according to the Social Security Administration.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

The Social Security Administration announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for 2027 . Beginning in January, benefits will rise by about $75 a month for the average retiree, the largest COLA increase in four years. Here's how to find out how much more you'll see in your own check next year.

The Social Security Administration will send COLA notices throughout December to Social Security and Social Security Income recipients, roughly 75 million beneficiaries in all.

Your exact new benefit won't be available until early December, when most beneficiaries can view their notice online.

You can find out exactly how much your benefits will increase by creating an account on SSA.gov ahead of time . After verifying your account, you'll be able to get an estimate of your retirement benefits and see how those benefits may change depending on your retirement age .

You'll receive notice of your exact adjustment in the "messages" tab within your SSA portal. To ensure you don't miss any news, select email or text notifications under message center preferences.

You can also estimate the change yourself and calculate your new Social Security benefit by multiplying the percentage increase by your current monthly benefit amount.

Say you're receiving $2,095, which is around the current average monthly benefit for retirees. When multiplied by 3.6% or 0.036, the new COLA, you can expect a monthly benefit in 2027 of about $2,170.42 — a $75.42 increase.

Leaving the workforce changes how you cover your day-to-day expenses. According to the SSA, Social Security benefits account for about 31% of income for people over age 65, and nearly 9 out of 10 Americans 65 and older receive Social Security.

With a modest monthly benefit, elevated interest rates, and higher food prices, it can be difficult for the average retired worker to make ends meet. However, there are ways you can stretch and supplement those benefits to accommodate your lifestyle.

Parking your Social Security payments, or a portion of them, in an interest-bearing account is an easy way to boost retiree benefits. In fact, many banks and credit unions are currently offering high-yield savings accounts with rates of up to 4%.

Retirees who can set aside a portion of their monthly Social Security check might benefit from a certificate of deposit (CD). Because you're committing to locking up your funds for a set period, banks and credit unions typically offer more lucrative APYs for these accounts.

A money market account is another type of account that generates interest, but unlike CDs, these accounts offer easier access to your funds through debit cards or check-writing privileges.

The annual COLA is based on the percentage increase in the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W). Data from the third quarter of the last year to the third quarter of the current year is used to calculate the COLA.

Making the most of your benefit checks starts with knowing exactly how much you'll receive.

Here's a primer on navigating the SSA website:

Setting up your My Social Security account is fairly straightforward and can be done at any time, whether retirement is months or years away.

Beneficiaries will need to provide their email address and at least one additional form of authentication, such as a phone number or a secondary email address, to verify their identity.

Next, you'll be asked for key information, including your Social Security number, your full name as it appears on your Social Security card, your date of birth, your address, and your phone number.

Once your account is set up, you can use it to manage your benefits, estimate your future benefits, request a Social Security card if you've lost yours, check the status of a benefits application, and more. You can also opt to receive all of your notices online, rather than by mail.

articles.title: Netflix Is Profitable and Still Growing. Why Did It Just Make a Huge Round of Layoffs and Oust Its Top Content Exec?
articles.summary: In 2025, Netflix notched a net profit of $11 billion on a 16% increase in revenue, to $46.6 billion. It expects revenue growth to cool off this year, project...
articles.body:
In 2025, Netflix notched a net profit of $11 billion on a 16% increase in revenue, to $46.6 billion. It expects revenue growth to cool off this year, projecting an increase of 13%-14%, while the streamer is aiming to boost operating margin by 200 basis points, to 31.5%. It has a healthy balance sheet, with $9.1 billion in cash and equivalents and very manageable total debt of $14.4 billion as of June 30.

So why did Netflix, which is still throwing off a good chunk of change, this week lay off around 1,000 employees — its biggest cutback to date?

Companies often make layoffs in crisis mode, such as when they're facing near-term revenue shortfalls and they simply can't make payroll. That's not the case here. But Netflix faces a festering pain point.

Specifically, investors are worried about the slowdown in its U.S./Canada region — which has raised questions about its long-term growth trajectory. For the second quarter of 2026, Netflix's UCAN revenue decelerated from 14% the prior quarter to 10% (partially due to its recent price hikes ). The company also issued Q3 revenue guidance below analyst expectations. Shares of Netflix are down 20% year-to-date on fears the streamer's days of double-digit gains are coming to an end.

Netflix's 6% reduction in force and the move to boot chief content officer Bela Bajaria — replacing her with well-regarded industry veteran Peter Rice, who hails from Disney and 21st Century Fox — signal its attempts to get in front of the issue.

Multiple industry sources told Variety they think Bajaria is being made the scapegoat for Netflix's larger problems. But content is the main engine that powers Netflix's financials. As Variety 's analysis of Bajaria's exit noted, Netflix hasn't produced a "culture-defining hit in the vein of 'Stranger Things' in quite some time."

Back to the all-important UCAN region: Total viewing hours in the U.S. and Canada declined in Q2, according to BMO Capital Markets analyst Brian Pitz. Netflix's parting ways with Bajaria and hiring Rice "suggest[s] to us that engagement trends may have softened further in 3Q26E," Pitz said in a research note Friday. The change in content leadership prompted the Wall Street firm to lower revenue estimates for Netflix's Q3 and Q4 by around 1% each and to also reduce its 2027 revenue forecast by 1.5%. BMO's model, Pitz added, "conservatively does not assume a UCAN revenue acceleration" until 2029.

articles.title: 8 countries, 42 nights, a new baby: How we did Europe on points and miles
articles.summary: Here's how I booked a six-week trip to Europe with my family of five using a combination of different credit card rewards for our flights and hotels.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

With a recent addition to our family and a generous parental leave policy, I was able to plan a six-week trip to Europe with my family of five, primarily using points and miles from travel credit cards . It gave my wife and me plenty of time to bond with our new son while exploring a collection of beautiful cities across eight different countries.

I knew increasing our family size by one could present some potential issues in Europe (I'm looking at you, European hotel rooms that tend to max out at four or fewer people), but we were still able to figure things out and have a resoundingly successful, though slightly tiring, trip.

Points, miles, and perks used: Choice Privileges: 330,000 points Flying Blue: 232,400 miles Hilton Honors (Diamond): 384,000 points + 3 Free Night Rewards Virgin Atlantic: 100,000 points World of Hyatt (Globalist): 475,000 points

Hilton Honors (Diamond): 384,000 points + 3 Free Night Rewards

World of Hyatt (Globalist): 475,000 points

Approximate cash value of rewards used: $51,264.98

Overall, this trip was slightly longer than our trip to Japan and Korea , and much longer than our all-inclusive visit to Mexico . In total, we visited eight countries, including France, Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, and the United Kingdom.

Note that the cash value of the rewards is approximate because prices can fluctuate and change, depending on when you check. However, in my experience, the gathered information provides a good, general look at what we may have saved by using credit card rewards rather than paying in cash for most of our flights and lodging.

Of course, I realize I would likely never pay $17,000 for business-class flights to Paris or more than $7,000 for a (relatively) short hotel stay in Cologne, but it's still fun and helpful to compare cash versus reward prices.

3 nights at Home Hotel Havnekontoret (two rooms)

3 nights at Hyatt Regency Mainz (two rooms)

5 nights at Hyatt Regency Cologne (two rooms)

5 nights at Hilton Brussels Grand Place (two rooms)

Which credit cards did we use to travel to Europe?

We didn't actually use American Express credit cards in Europe because they aren't accepted everywhere, but they were essential for planning and booking our trip. Specifically, we used a lot of Amex Membership Rewards points and Hilton Honors points on this trip, all earned from these cards:

We used the Capital One Venture X as one of our main spenders while in Europe, as it doesn't charge foreign transaction fees and has a well-balanced rewards rate for all types of purchases.

We used the Chase Sapphire Preferred as a backup to the Capital One Venture X.

We didn't actually use this on our trip, but the World of Hyatt Credit Card helped us earn Hyatt points and maintain Globalist status, both of which were useful during our stays at Hyatt hotels.

We had no intention of using this on our trip, but it came in handy when none of our Visa cards worked to book a G7 taxi in Paris. This is a Mastercard, and it worked like a charm.

We don't currently have a Citi Strata Premier Card, but both my wife and I used to, and the points we earned previously went toward our Choice Privileges hotel bookings in Scandinavia on this trip.

This isn't a credit card, but we always bring our Charles Schwab debit card with us when traveling internationally because it reimburses foreign ATM fees. We found we didn't need much cash on this trip, but it's always nice to have it just in case.

My strategy for booking flights to Europe using credit card rewards

Our available rewards typically guide my trip plans, and we had plenty of Amex and Chase points to spare. We also knew we wanted to go to Europe, and our closest airports are Salt Lake City (SLC) and Las Vegas (LAS), which led me to consider Air France, KLM, and Virgin Atlantic as direct-flight options to Paris (CDG), Amsterdam (AMS), and London (LHR).

I knew business-class flights to/from Europe were fairly common with Air France-KLM Flying Blue, so I checked flights just about every day until I found a flight to Paris that would fit our schedule and available rewards. I had also found Upper Class flights with Virgin Atlantic from London to get home, but I really wanted to avoid paying $3,000+ in taxes and fees when leaving the U.K., so we opted for Delta economy on the return flight.

With the flights booked, we could build the rest of our itinerary, which is typically how we like to plan out our trips. When the first flight is booked, we can start looking into hotels and (possibly) short or mid-trip flights.

And we ended up with two mid-trip flights. We booked flights from Paris to Copenhagen, then from Bergen to Düsseldorf. We would have preferred to use trains, but it didn't make sense for these parts of the itinerary. We used Flying Blue miles for the Copenhagen flight and then applied our $300 Capital One Travel credit (from the Capital One Venture X) to help pay for the Düsseldorf flight.

My strategy for booking hotels and other lodging in Europe

Once we had our flight to Europe booked, we started planning out our trip itinerary and hotels. We had plenty of Chase points to spare, which meant we (indirectly) had plenty of Hyatt points. We were also sitting on a stack of Choice points.

Originally, we wanted to travel solely around France, spending a lot of time in the countryside with our young kids and generally enjoying castle visits, food, and everything in between. However, the route we had from Paris down to the French Riviera didn't exactly jive with our available rewards, so we eventually nixed that idea and started looking elsewhere.

Our stack of Choice points led us to Scandinavia, an area we have wanted to visit for a while but one we knew would be expensive. Fortunately, Choice points can take you far in Denmark, Sweden, and Norway and can even cover some of your food expenses along the way.

The Home Hotel brand, in particular, provided both breakfast and dinner, which was fantastic in Gothenburg and Bergen.

We used our stack of Hyatt points in France, Germany, and the U.K., and our Hyatt Globalist status got us free breakfast and executive lounge access where available. Unfortunately, a family of five doesn't always meet European occupancy limits, so we had to book multiple rooms at German hotels, which used a lot more points than we'd wanted to.

For our stop in Brussels, we opted to use Hilton points and Free Night Awards at the very conveniently located Hilton Brussels Grand Place. Our Hilton Honors Diamond status got us free breakfast and access to the executive lounge, which was nice. However, again, we had to book two rooms because our family wouldn't fit in just one.

Note that we also had a couple of non-points stays, including three nights in Oslo and three nights at the Efteling theme park in the Netherlands. We had run short of Choice points for Oslo, so we decided to book an Airbnb using accumulated account credit from discounted gift cards we had previously purchased.

Unfortunately, there aren't too many ways to book an Efteling stay using credit card rewards, so we just paid for three nights at the Efteling Wonder Hotel, which was easily one of the highlights of our entire trip. It was a hassle to get there from Cologne with all our luggage, and then another hassle to get to Brussels afterward, but we loved our visit, so it was worth it.

Breakdown of the points and miles we redeemed for this trip

3-night stay (2 rooms) at Home Hotel Havnekontoret

Citi ThankYou Rewards and Amex Membership Rewards transfers

5-night stay (2 rooms) at Hilton Brussels Grand Place

5-night stay at Hyatt Regency Paris Etoile

3-night stay (2 rooms) at Hyatt Regency Mainz

5-night stay (2 rooms) at Hyatt Regency Cologne

Chase Ultimate Rewards transfers and World of Hyatt credit cards

Tips and tricks for visiting Europe as a family of five

Young children often travel for free on public transport in many European cities and countries, so be sure to check whether that's an option to save money on your trip.

You can get around Europe by train, plane, or car. We typically enjoy renting cars so we can travel at our own pace and stop wherever we want, but we had no desire to lug car seats around on this trip, and it was difficult to figure out how to source affordable car seats after arrival.

So, we mostly used trains, which is another of our preferred modes of transportation. We also did a few intra-Europe flights.

Your European itinerary may look a bit different, but just remember that there are various ways to get around, so don't limit yourself. We dealt with the usual number of train delays and a frustrating situation where we almost missed our flight to Copenhagen, but fortunately, everything worked out just fine.

Note: Depending on the popularity of certain train routes, you may need to book tickets and seat reservations early. I made the mistake of waiting to book our seven-hour scenic train ride from Oslo to Bergen, and all the good times were already sold out. This meant we had to adjust our schedule, including rescheduling a fjord cruise.

Everyone has different ways of traveling, and I realize that not everyone has six weeks to spend in Europe. We thought we were spreading ourselves just fine across the trip — when we were really spreading ourselves a bit thin.

For example, our stretch of three nights each in Oslo, Bergen, and Mainz was very fast-paced, especially when you account for little kids, including a literal baby, and long travel days. You only get two full days when you have three nights, so you really want to pack in activities, but you're tired from the traveling you already did to arrive at your new destination.

This can make for long days, which is why we much prefer four- or five-night stays, particularly if we're visiting a major city or destination with plenty to do.

We get free phone data in most countries around the world with our T-Mobile plan, but it's limited to a certain amount of high-speed data per month, after which it slows down a lot. Even after the data slows down, it's still usually good enough for limited web browsing and Google Maps searches. But I just didn't want to deal with slow data, so I bought eSIMs for both my wife and me.

We used two different providers, Ubigi and RedteaGO, and they both worked well throughout the trip, though one sometimes performed better than the other depending on the location.

I think it's worth paying the small price for an eSIM if it's compatible with your phone, especially if your only alternative is the travel data option from your U.S. carrier, which typically costs an arm and a leg.

We used our credit cards for just about everything. We originally got some cash in Paris and brought some pounds from another trip to use in London, but we only needed cash in a few situations.

Specifically, I did have to use cash a few times at laundromats in different countries, though some accepted cards. And there was also an international food event in Oslo one day where you needed either a local payment app or cash to pay for food. Apart from that, we pretty much only used cash so we could get rid of it and wouldn't have to take it home.

Keep in mind that you want a credit card with no foreign transaction fees if you're going to travel abroad. In addition, Visa and Mastercard are typically the most accepted payment networks.

I like to carry both options on me just in case, and this preparation actually worked out almost immediately when I was trying to book a G7 taxi from the Paris airport (CDG) and my Visa cards weren't working, but the one Mastercard in my wallet worked just fine.

My Google Maps is littered with saved playgrounds across Europe because young kids can only do so much walking around fancy buildings and gardens until they get sick of it and just need to play.

As a side note, marking bathrooms around different attractions also helped when nature inevitably called.

Booking a Europe trip on points and miles FAQs

What is the best way to fly to Europe using points and miles?

It depends on where you live and what rewards you have, but major European cities like Dublin, London, Amsterdam, Paris, Madrid, and Lisbon have plenty of direct flights and award availability from U.S. cities.

This could include using airline programs such as Aer Lingus, British Airways, Delta, Iberia, KLM-Air France Flying Blue, Virgin Atlantic, and others to book your flights. This is especially true if you already have transferable rewards from a credit card program like Amex Membership Rewards, Capital One miles, or Chase Ultimate Rewards.

Is $5,000 enough for two weeks in Europe?

It can be, but it depends entirely on your itinerary and travel preferences. If this is your budget after accounting for flights and lodging, that should be more than enough for both food and attractions in most locations if you aren't splurging. If this includes flights and lodging, you would likely need to be stricter with your daily budget.

What are the cheapest countries to visit in Europe?

Eastern Europe is typically cheaper than Western Europe, so visiting countries like Albania, Serbia, and Romania often yields lower prices for lodging and meals. You can also include more Central European countries like Poland and Hungary, while the traditionally popular countries like France, Italy, and Spain are more expensive, though it depends on where you visit.

How early should I book award flights to Europe?

I recommend booking the flights you want as early as you can. With business-class flights, availability can be sparse, depending on the airline and route, so it's best to book early. For economy awards, you generally have a bit more flexibility with your options.

I've been using credit card rewards for more than 15 years, solely to make my travels more affordable. This crazy hobby, passion, and, eventually, career has been with me since I was a single college student, a new husband, and now, somehow, a dad of three.

I understand that it can be a lot to take in, especially when you're just starting out, but I hope you hang in there because the rewards can be well worth the effort. As long as you approach rewards credit cards with the mindset that you're using them to make purchases you'd make anyway — and you're always going to pay them off before interest accrues — they can be extremely beneficial for both their rewards and credit-building opportunities.

articles.title: Southwest just updated Rapid Rewards: What to know about the new elite status tiers
articles.summary: Southwest just revamped its Rapid Rewards program for 2027. Here’s what to know if you’re a frequent Southwest traveler.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

Southwest Airlines is overhauling its Rapid Rewards loyalty program with new elite status tiers, changes to its much-loved Companion Pass benefit, and more.

Starting Jan. 1, 2027, Southwest ( LUV ) will simplify its rewards currencies and replace its A-List and A-List Preferred tiers with Silver, Gold, and Platinum status. Members will also be able to earn new Milestone Rewards and will have new options for scoring a Companion Pass.

This is the latest in a series of big changes the airline has made recently.

Earlier this year, Southwest eliminated its popular "Two bags fly free" policy and introduced assigned seating on flights. Last year, Southwest Rapid Rewards credit cards got revamped with higher annual fees and updated benefits. Now, Southwest is transforming the Rapid Rewards program as a whole.

"As our members engage more with Southwest, they've told us they want Rapid Rewards to reward them in more meaningful ways," Nandika Suri, vice president of Rapid Rewards at Southwest Airlines, said in an announcement. "These updates build on that feedback by rewarding Members throughout their Southwest experience, while keeping the simplicity and value that have always set our program apart."

Here are some highlights coming to Rapid Rewards in 2027:

New Southwest Rapid Rewards elite status tiers

The new Southwest Rapid Rewards elite status tiers are Silver, Gold, and Platinum.

Silver replaces A-List status, and Gold replaces A-List Preferred status. Many benefits for existing status members will remain the same, including priority boarding, a free checked bag, seat selection, and more.

One big difference for the new Silver and Gold tiers is how travelers earn status:

Silver status: 35,000 TQPs or 25 qualifying one-way flights That's the same number of TQPs but 5 more qualifying flights than it previously took to earn A-List status.

Silver status: 35,000 TQPs or 25 qualifying one-way flights

That's the same number of TQPs but 5 more qualifying flights than it previously took to earn A-List status.

Gold status: 65,000 TQPs or 50 qualifying one-way flights That's 5,000 fewer TQPs than previously required to earn A-List Preferred status, but 10 additional qualifying flights.

Gold status: 65,000 TQPs or 50 qualifying one-way flights

That's 5,000 fewer TQPs than previously required to earn A-List Preferred status, but 10 additional qualifying flights.

The new Rapid Rewards program will also include a new tier: Platinum . Platinum status requires earning 140,000 TQPs in a calendar year or taking 100 qualifying one-way flights.

Platinum is the most premium Rapid Rewards tier. Its perks include priority boarding before Gold status members and Group 1, three free checked bags, a 120% earning bonus on qualifying flights, and more.

One of the most valuable Platinum perks is unlimited Companion Pass trips. Platinum status holders can bring one designated companion for free (excluding taxes and fees) on any flight.

In addition to new status tiers, Southwest is also introducing Milestone Rewards. Similar to earning status, these rewards apply after reaching a certain number of TQPs or taking a certain number of qualifying flights.

Milestone Rewards are separate from elite status, but they offer additional perks for members working toward status tiers.

There are two Milestone Rewards you can earn in 2027:

First milestone: Earn 20,000 TQPs or take 15 qualifying one-way flights Rapid Rewards members can earn this milestone on their way to Silver status. After qualifying, travelers can choose a reward of either 20,000 Rapid Rewards points to put toward award flights or two Preferred Seat Certificates to use on upcoming flights.

First milestone: Earn 20,000 TQPs or take 15 qualifying one-way flights

Rapid Rewards members can earn this milestone on their way to Silver status. After qualifying, travelers can choose a reward of either 20,000 Rapid Rewards points to put toward award flights or two Preferred Seat Certificates to use on upcoming flights.

Second milestone: Earn 95,000 TQPs or take 75 qualifying one-way flights Rapid Rewards members can earn this milestone after claiming Gold status and before reaching Platinum status. This milestone comes with three Companion Pass trips.

Second milestone: Earn 95,000 TQPs or take 75 qualifying one-way flights

Rapid Rewards members can earn this milestone after claiming Gold status and before reaching Platinum status. This milestone comes with three Companion Pass trips.

Under the new Rapid Rewards program, earning TQPs or taking qualifying flights is the best way to earn a Companion Pass.

To get unlimited Companion Pass trips, travelers will need to earn Platinum elite status. But Gold status members who earn the second Milestone Reward on their way to Platinum can earn three Companion Pass trips.

Previously, Southwest Rapid Rewards members could get Companion Pass after earning 135,000 Companion Pass qualifying points or taking 100 qualifying one-way flights.

The new program eliminates Companion Pass qualifying points. Now, travelers earn the same Tier Qualifying Points (TQPs) toward Companion Pass and elite status. These points come from taking Southwest flights and Southwest Rapid Rewards credit card spending.

However, some previous strategies to boost qualifying points will no longer count toward qualifying for Companion Pass. That includes credit card welcome bonuses, anniversary points, and bonus rewards on card spending. Instead, for every $1 spent using a Rapid Rewards credit card, members will earn one TQP.

Current Southwest travelers who earn Companion Pass in 2026 under the existing program will still maintain their Companion Pass benefits through the end of 2027.

What the new program means for Southwest flyers

The new program simplifies some aspects of earning status with the airline, while also making it potentially more difficult for some travelers to earn status and Companion Pass.

Rapid Rewards credit cardholders may get the biggest boost. Not every card earns TQPs today, but starting in 2027, every dollar spent on a Rapid Rewards credit card will earn one TQP. That means cardholders may have the fastest path to reaching elite status tiers.

Cardholders will also continue to earn Rapid Rewards points (including bonus points) on their purchases, which they can use toward award flights with the airline.

However, even cardholders may find it more difficult to earn Southwest's coveted Companion Pass. Eliminating Companion Pass qualifying points means that welcome bonuses and anniversary points won't count toward the pass. Only the biggest spenders or most frequent flyers who qualify for Platinum elite status will unlock unlimited Companion Pass trips under the new program.

These rewards program changes are only some of the continued updates Southwest is making in 2027. Later in the year, members will have the option to earn and redeem rewards with partner travel programs (including Icelandair, Etihad Airways, and more) and redeem points for upgraded seats after booking. The airline has also teased upcoming airport lounges and a new premium credit card that offers lounge access.

articles.title: Grão de MG bate recorde em leilão no Japão, por mais de R$ 2 mil o kg | G1
articles.standfirst: Para agricultor, marco mostra que o Brasil tem potencial de produzir os melhores cafés do mundo. Fazenda mineira é considerada uma lenda do setor e já ganhou prêmio equivalente ao 'Oscar'.
articles.summary: Para agricultor, marco mostra que o Brasil tem potencial de produzir os melhores cafés do mundo. Fazenda mineira é considerada uma lenda do setor.
articles.body:
Produtor Luiz Paulo ao lado de Nara Byun, representante da empresa compradora Snow Beans Coffe — Foto: Reprodução / Redes sociais

Você pagaria mais de R$ 2.000 por um quilo de café? Um café produzido em Minas Gerais bateu essa marca: a saca de 60 kg foi vendida por US$ 26.456, o equivalente a R$ 134.581,67 , durante o SCAJ 2026 — World Specialty Coffee Conference and Exhibition, evento organizado pela Associação de Cafés Especiais do Japão, em Tóquio .

O valor foi o maior já alcançado por um café brasileiro em leilões da Alliance for Coffee Excellence (ACE).

🔍 A Alliance for Coffee Excellence reúne produtores reconhecidos como lendas do setor por cultivarem cafés de qualidade excepcional e acumularem diversos prêmios do Cup of Excellence, o "Oscar" do setor. Apenas seis países fazem parte: Brasil, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Honduras, Guatemala e Nicarágua.

A Fazenda Santuário Sul, em Carmo de Minas, é considerada uma referência brasileira na produção de cafés especiais e já foi premiada no "Oscar" do setor.

A compra foi feita pela empresa japonesa Snow Beans Coffee durante o leilão na sexta-feira (16).

Para o produtor Luiz Paulo Dias Pereira Filho, o resultado do leilão é fruto de um trabalho que leva meses.

Ele explica que a variedade cultivada, a geisha natural, tem grande potencial de produção e dá à bebida um sabor floral, com notas de jasmim e mamão papaia. O resultado é um café mais doce e delicado ao paladar.

O cafeicultor acredita que a localização da propriedade também contribuiu para a valorização do grão. O município fica nas montanhas da Serra da Mantiqueira, região de clima ameno.

O preço alcançado no leilão, de US$ 200 por libra-peso, representa uma alta de 40% em relação ao recorde brasileiro anterior, registrado em 2018. Na época, o produto foi vendido por US$ 143 por libra-peso, totalizando US$ 18,9 mil por saca de 60 kg, cerca de R$ 96,2 mil.

Embora Pereira seja da quarta geração da família a trabalhar com café, o investimento em cafés especiais começou nos anos 2000. Segundo ele, o objetivo é levar o produto brasileiro para o mundo.

"Eles [a família] sempre acreditaram que, realmente, o café era um produto sem fronteira", afirma.

"Dividir essa vitória com o Brasil. Mostrar que a gente pode valorizar o nosso produto e, principalmente, que o mercado reconhece que o Brasil tem potencial de produzir os melhores cafés do mundo", completa.

articles.title: Frango chinês até 20% mais barato desafia o Brasil  | G1
articles.standfirst: País ampliou a produção de alimentos, mas o consumo interno perdeu força. Agora, empresas chinesas buscam clientes no exterior e pressionam exportadores tradicionais.
articles.summary: Com produção acima da demanda interna, empresas chinesas ampliam vendas no exterior e conquistam compradores com preços de 10% a 20% menores que os do frango brasileiro.
articles.body:
Como mostrou o g1 nesta semana, a China está produzindo mais carne e laticínios do que consegue consumir, e o excedente está sendo exportado. Com preços mais baixos e investimentos em tecnologia, empresas chinesas avançam sobre mercados tradicionalmente abastecidos por países como o Brasil.

O movimento é resultado de uma mudança no consumo interno e de uma estratégia do governo chinês para ampliar a segurança alimentar. Nos últimos anos, o país incentivou a expansão da produção agropecuária, mas a demanda doméstica perdeu força, criando um excesso de oferta.

Dados alfandegários mostrados pela agência Reuters mostram agora que a China exportou US$ 2,6 bilhões em produtos de frango em 2025, quase o dobro do valor registrado em 2020.

No ano passado, o país também se tornou exportador líquido de carne de frango, ou seja, passou a exportar mais do que importar o produto.

Durante décadas, a carne suína foi a principal proteína da dieta chinesa. Houve uma redução do consumo de porco, especialmente entre moradores de áreas urbanas, que passaram a dar mais espaço a outras opções, como o frango.

O consumo per capita de carne suína caiu 13% desde o pico registrado em 2023, segundo dados oficiais e informações da imprensa estatal chinesa. Na direção contrária, o consumo de frango por pessoa aumentou mais de 50% na década encerrada em 2024.

Mesmo com a mudança nos hábitos alimentares e a desaceleração da economia, a produção continuou crescendo. Em 2025, a China produziu um recorde de 59 milhões de toneladas de carne suína, enquanto a produção de aves avançou 7%.

Frango chinês chega a custar até 20% menos que o brasileiro

Com a oferta elevada, os produtores chineses passaram a buscar compradores no exterior. A vantagem de preço tem ajudado as empresas a conquistar clientes em mercados antes abastecidos por exportadores tradicionais.

Segundo Ezequiel Pires, presidente da comerciante internacional de carnes Branexx, cortes chineses de peito e coxa de frango custam de 10% a 20% menos que os produtos brasileiros. A empresa começou a comprar aves da China em março, depois que clientes africanos procuraram alternativas mais baratas às importações do Brasil.

Na Tailândia, um dos principais concorrentes da China no setor, a expansão das vendas chinesas também preocupa. Representantes da indústria local afirmam que compradores têm usado os preços chineses como referência para negociar com outros fornecedores.

Exportações chinesas avançam em mercados tradicionais

A expansão já aparece nos dados de comércio internacional. A participação da China no mercado de produtos de aves processadas da União Europeia dobrou desde 2022, chegando a 10%. No Reino Unido, a fatia chinesa triplicou e superou 14%, segundo dados da consultoria Gira citados pela Reuters.

O avanço aumenta a concorrência para produtores europeus e asiáticos e pode pressionar exportadores brasileiros que disputam os mesmos compradores internacionais.

Além do frango, as empresas chinesas também ampliam as vendas de laticínios. As exportações desses produtos devem alcançar US$ 600 milhões em 2026, o dobro do valor registrado três anos antes, segundo dados citados pela Reuters.

Subsídios e produção em larga escala ajudam a reduzir custos

A expansão da produção chinesa foi estimulada por políticas de segurança alimentar e incentivos a grandes empresas agropecuárias. O objetivo era aumentar a oferta interna e recuperar rebanhos após crises sanitárias, como o surto de peste suína africana de 2018.

Entre 2022 e 2024, os subsídios representaram cerca de 13% da receita bruta dos produtores agrícolas chineses, quase três vezes o nível registrado no início dos anos 2000, segundo a Organização para a Cooperação e Desenvolvimento Econômico (OCDE).

Na avicultura, empresas também investiram em instalações maiores e em processos mais eficientes. Uma das companhias ouvidas pela Reuters, a Wintop Food, aumentou de 20 mil para 120 mil o número de frangos alojados em cada galpão ao longo de uma década.

Preço baixo ainda precisa superar desconfiança sobre qualidade

Apesar do avanço comercial, a indústria chinesa ainda enfrenta dúvidas relacionadas ao histórico de escândalos de segurança alimentar no país. Para consolidar as exportações, os produtores precisam demonstrar que seus produtos atendem aos padrões sanitários e mantêm qualidade e rastreabilidade consistentes.

Na União Europeia, os alimentos importados devem cumprir as mesmas exigências sanitárias e de segurança aplicadas aos produtos locais. O bloco também planeja reforçar a identificação da origem dos alimentos, começando por produtos de aves em 2027.

Para os compradores internacionais, porém, o preço continua sendo um fator decisivo. A combinação de produção em larga escala, oferta excedente e custos competitivos pode ampliar a presença chinesa no comércio global de proteínas e aumentar a disputa com exportadores tradicionais, como o Brasil.

articles.title: ‘Much appreciated:’ Musk on Reliance Starlink stand as Rubio set to meet Ambani
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Elon Musk’s blow hot and cold stand for getting Starlink access to India has now entered a conciliatory phase after the tech trillionaire was
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Elon Musk’s blow hot and cold stand for getting Starlink access to India has now entered a conciliatory phase after the tech trillionaire was all fire on X last week. The change in tone comes at a time when US secretary of state Marco Rubio is in India and will visit the world’s largest oil refinery in Jamnagar that’s owned by Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani — who was targeted by Musk last week.“Much appreciated,” Musk said on X late Friday night in response to Reliance Industries first reply to his charges on Friday, where Mukesh Ambani’s conglomerate had said: “We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink. Every player, Jio included, must… abide by the laws and policies of the land…. As govt of India has stated, it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign. Jio's own satellite services await clearances.”Starlink also responded to Reliance post, saying it has “worked closely with regulators, industry and operators in India for five plus years, and built a network of dedicated systems, gateways, and other infrastructure all in-country to exclusively serve Indian traffic safely and securely and all with the requisite government approvals. Starlink is ready to connect India with high-speed internet.”Sunil Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb, Ambani’s Reliance Jio and Musk’s Starlink have got licences and are preparing to start satcom service here so that even remote areas where laying ground infra for broadband is not possible can get the same. Billionaire Jeff Bezos-led Amazon's Project Kuiper is eying a licence to do so.Starlink clearance is being seen as part of the larger Indo-US ties with several factors being part of the play including the trade deal and threat of tariffs over buying Russian oil.Sunil Bharti Mittal had this Wednesday said the company was significantly ahead of Starlink in securing approvals for satellite communications services in India. “We are already waiting for approvals, I am significantly ahead, we got our approvals five years back, so I will be happy to get my approvals a few days before it (Starlink),” Mittal had said at an event.Reliance Jio has proposed a constellation of around 1,600 Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites and 23 ground stations to provide sovereign satellite internet connectivity across India.Last Wednesday, Musk had accused “certain oligarchs” of “blocking” Starlink’s entry to India without naming anyone but saying “you can guess who they are” and then named Ambani over the next two days in a series of X posts.You use AI every day. articles.title: Morgan Stanley sees risk asset bull market regaining momentum as growth, AI support returns
articles.summary: Global markets could see risk assets regain momentum as strong economic growth, rising corporate earnings and AI-led productivity support returns despite
articles.body: Global markets could see risk assets regain momentum as strong economic growth, rising corporate earnings and AI-led productivity support returns despite higher bond yields, according to a Morgan Stanley report.The firm now favours global stocks over bonds, saying rising bond yields reflect a strong economy rather than a worsening economic situation.“As the forces driving yields higher begin to fade, we expect the bull market in risk assets to reassert itself,” the report said.Morgan Stanley said stronger economic growth continues to underpin corporate earnings, cash flows, employment, consumption and credit quality. Meanwhile, the adoption of and investment in artificial intelligence (AI) remain key drivers of productivity gains and business expansion.Global economic activity has remained firm despite higher energy prices and interest rates, with services and manufacturing activity showing signs of acceleration, the report noted.Productivity gains could also help wages and output grow without a corresponding increase in labour costs, potentially helping contain inflationary pressures.Oil supply shock remains a key riskDespite its constructive outlook, Morgan Stanley cautioned that geopolitical tensions, energy supply disruptions and persistent inflation could threaten the market's momentum.The report identified an oil supply shock that forces central banks to tighten monetary policy excessively as a key risk to its positive outlook for risk assets.“If inflation becomes uncontained, central banks must move from removing accommodation to actively destroying demand,” the report said.It also warned that refined oil products, particularly diesel, remain vulnerable to supply disruptions. Any such disruption could push energy costs higher and feed into inflation.While the firm expects economic growth to remain supportive of risk assets, a sustained energy shock could change its outlook.US equities preferred, India faces challengesWithin equities, Morgan Stanley maintained its overweight position on US markets, citing resilient economic growth, strong corporate earnings and continued AI adoption.The firm remained cautious on European equities because of energy-related headwinds, although it identified opportunities in the banking and utilities sectors.Indian equities, meanwhile, face challenges from comparatively weaker forward earnings growth expectations, limited exposure to AI and elevated energy prices, the report said.Morgan Stanley said the balance of risks remained constructive for now. However, the outlook will depend on whether economic resilience and productivity gains can continue to offset the effects of higher energy prices and inflation.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Huge growth potential for visitors from India:’ VisitBritain CEO Patricia Yates
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: With a huge Indian diaspora, the United Kingdom is betting big on boosting travel from the country.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With a huge Indian diaspora, the United Kingdom is betting big on boosting travel from the country. Patricia Yates, CEO of VisitBritain which is UK’s national tourism agency, says the Indian market is expected to be worth about £1.5 billion by 2030, up from £865 million this year with the number of visitors seeing rising from current under 6 lakh to almost 10 lakh in this time period.“While the average length of stay in the UK of an international visitor is seven days, guests from India stay for 28 days. The average spend per international visitor is £800 and for Indians it is at £1,300,” Yates told TOI.The UK, as expected like most western countries, has seen its visitor numbers getting affected by the ongoing West Asia crisis as a lot of connectivity comes via the hubs there, especially from India. As of now, it is Europe that is proving to be “growth driver” for it.While Indian visitors flock to Scotland and Wales also, the north of England has set its eyes on attracting them in large numbers. Kim McGuinness, North East Mayor and Chair of The Great North, said: “We want Indian visitors to enjoy everything Britain has to offer, but to travel further, stay longer and experience more. From our great cities and spectacular landscapes to Premier League football, international cricket, castles, culture and coastline, the North has an incredible amount to offer.”Steve Rotheram, mayor of the Liverpool City Region, said: “The Liverpool City Region has so much to offer Indian visitors. We’re the UK’s cultural capital, home to The Beatles, two Premier League football clubs and an internationally renowned music, arts and cultural scene. As the UK’s third most visited region by international visitors, our visitor economy generates almost £7 billion a year and supports more than 58,000 local jobs. And beyond the world-class attractions, there’s nowhere quite like Liverpool when it comes to the warmth of our welcome. India’s growing tourism market presents a fantastic opportunity for the entire North.”Tracy Brabin, mayor of West Yorkshire, said, “From Bronte Country to bustling nightlife, Hepworth to Hockney, West Yorkshire has so much culture at its heart. Across Yorkshire, tourism, including screen tourism, is worth a whopping £9 billion every year. As the partnership of the Great North, we can showcase our spectacular sights, vibrant culture, and encourage more people to explore our regions.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Crude oil prices may fall to $80 in 2027: What could bring prices down?
articles.summary: The global oil market could move from a supply crunch towards a surplus by the end of 2026, paving the way for lower crude prices next year, Goldman Sachs
articles.body: The global oil market could move from a supply crunch towards a surplus by the end of 2026, paving the way for lower crude prices next year, Goldman Sachs Research has said.The firm expects Brent crude to average $80 per barrel in 2027, provided supplies from the Middle East continue to recover and demand gradually improves.The forecast comes even as oil prices remain under pressure from the risk of further escalation in the US-Israel-Iran conflict. Goldman Sachs warned that renewed hostilities could prolong supply disruptions and delay the expected moderation in prices.Daan Struyven, co-head of global commodities research and head of oil research at Goldman Sachs, said the firm now expects Brent crude to reach $90 per barrel in December 2026. This is higher than its earlier projection of $85 per barrel. For 2027, however, the bank expects prices to average $80 per barrel.The changing outlook follows a sharp reduction in the gap between global oil demand and supply. In March, demand outstripped supply by 7.2 million barrels per day (mb/d). By September, the shortfall had narrowed to just 0.3 mb/d.Goldman Sachs attributed the improvement to three factors: the recovery in Middle Eastern oil exports, increased production outside the Persian Gulf and weaker consumption. Based on these trends, the bank expects supply to exceed demand in the fourth quarter of 2026, with the surplus continuing into 2027.Middle East exports recover, but risks remainOil shipments from the Persian Gulf have shown signs of recovery despite the conflict. Goldman Sachs estimated that exports from the region had returned to around their 2025 average by late September, as exporters adapted to the situation and expanded transportation capacity.However, the improvement in supply has not eliminated concerns about further disruptions. Physical Brent prices for near-term delivery have risen above $130 per barrel, while benchmark Brent futures have recently traded above $100."Physical prices remain elevated because escalation threatens supply while near-record-low global inventories fuel strong restocking demand," Struyven said, as cited by ANI.Goldman Sachs estimates that the possibility of further disruptions is adding nearly $25 per barrel to crude prices in the form of a risk premium. The premium also reflects the prospect of additional inventory drawdowns if the conflict intensifies.Weak consumption weighs on the outlookDemand has also played a significant role in easing pressure on the global oil market. Consumption in the third quarter of 2026 was 3.3 mb/d lower than in the corresponding period a year earlier. China, the Middle East and developed Asian economies accounted for much of the weakness.The bank expects consumption to recover gradually as refined oil products become more available and affordable. Nevertheless, it does not expect demand to return fully to the level it might have reached in the absence of the conflict-related shock.In the fourth quarter of 2027, global oil demand is projected to remain 0.7 mb/d below that hypothetical trajectory. Goldman Sachs attributed part of the gap to faster adoption of electric vehicles and changes in fuel consumption patterns in China.The outlook for oil prices will therefore hinge on how quickly production and exports recover, how demand normalises and whether the conflict in the Middle East escalates again. While the anticipated supply surplus supports the bank's forecast of lower prices in 2027, renewed disruptions could keep crude elevated for longer than expected.You use AI every day. articles.title: You earn, save and invest. But are you financially literate? 10 questions to ask
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: \"Understand before you invest.\" Many must have received a message from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) through its awareness
articles.body: NEW DELHI: "Understand before you invest." Many must have received a message from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) through its awareness initiative, "Samajh Se Investing Simple".But how much do you really need to know about money and investment? This is where financial literacy comes in. And of course, it goes well beyond knowing how to buy shares or start a systematic investment plan (SIP). It involves understanding where your money goes, how borrowing works, what risks investments carry, how inflation affects savings and why taxes matter.Financial literacy is a “combination of financial awareness, knowledge, skills, attitude and behaviour necessary to make sound financial decisions and ultimately achieve individual financial well being,” as defined by the organisation for economic co-operation and development (OECD), an international organisation that works with governments to develop policies for better economic and social outcomes.And as India's investor base expands, an important question emerges: Are more people becoming financially literate, or are they simply gaining easier access to financial products? Or just following the hype and the crowd?According to the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI), the mutual fund industry had 28.62 crore folios as of September 30, 2026, while assets under management stood at Rs 82.64 lakh crore. Participation in the stock market has also expanded rapidly. The National Stock Exchange (NSE) reported more than 25 crore registered client accounts as of February 2026, with its unique registered investor base crossing 13 crore in April 2026. Meanwhile, the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) added 3.53 crore investor accounts in FY26, taking its total beyond 25 crore.The shift is also visible in how households allocate their savings. The Economic Survey 2025-26 showed a gradual shift towards equity and investment funds in the composition of household financial assets from FY19 to FY25.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();The gap between participation and understanding becomes more apparent when investors' knowledge is examined. The Sebi Investor Survey 2025 found that only 36 per cent of investors had high or moderate knowledge of the securities market. The assessment tested respondents' familiarity with stock markets and their understanding of how inflation affects purchasing power. The findings raise an important question: as more Indians enter financial markets, are they equipped to understand the products they buy and the risks they take?So, how financially literate are you? There is no formal set of rules to define it, but here are 10 questions that can help determine it with expert insights.1. Do you know where your money goes every month?Financial literacy begins with understanding your income, expenses and savings. Can you identify how much you spend on essentials, discretionary purchases and debt repayments? Do you know how much remains for emergencies and future goals?A budget need not be complicated. Even a monthly record of earnings and expenses can help identify unnecessary spending.2. Do you understand inflation and compounding?Suppose you have Rs 1 lakh today. If inflation averages 5 per cent annually, something costing Rs 1 lakh today would cost approximately Rs 1.63 lakh after 10 years.That is why keeping money aside is not always enough. You must also consider whether your savings and investments can preserve purchasing power.Compounding, meanwhile, allows returns to generate further returns over time. But the same principle can work against borrowers when unpaid interest accumulates.Understanding both concepts helps explain why starting early, staying consistent, and managing debt are important.In this regard, Aswini Bajaj, CEO of Leveraged Growth, cautioned against blindly following popular savings formulas. "Understanding the fundamentals is important, but knowing how to apply them to your own life matters just as much. The goal is to make informed financial decisions based on your needs and circumstances, rather than blindly following thumb rules or someone else's advice."Further encouraging people to understand finance better, he added, “Whether you’re earning your first salary, starting to invest or feeling the pressure to match a lifestyle you see on social media, ask yourself: What am I saving or investing for?” He further stressed that the focus should be on using money to achieve personal goals and build financial security, rather than chasing returns or following trends without assessing their suitability.3. Can you distinguish between saving and investing?Saving generally involves setting money aside for immediate needs, emergencies or short-term goals. Investing involves committing money to assets with the expectation of generating returns, usually while accepting some degree of risk.As CA Balvinder Singh Oberoi stressed, earning more is not enough; what matters is how well people save and make their money work for them. “Buying and selling shares on any app doesn't make anyone literate,” he said, emphasising that investments must be aligned with financial goals rather than treated as an end in themselves.Oberoi also highlighted the gap between knowing the importance of saving and actually practising it, pointing to lifestyle inflation, the desire for instant gratification and intimidating financial jargon as barriers to financial discipline.Ultimately, financial literacy means understanding your assets and liabilities, knowing when and where to deploy your money, and making financial decisions that support your goals and long-term wealth creation.4. Do you understand risk before investing?Every investment carries risks, although their nature and extent differ.Stocks can fluctuate sharply, mutual funds are subject to market risks, and even relatively stable products can carry inflation, liquidity or other risks.Before investing, ask whether you understand the product, its potential losses, charges and suitability for your financial goals.Leveraged Growth CEO Bajaj thus made an important distinction between the ability to bear losses and the emotional willingness to accept them. "Being able to afford risk and being comfortable with it are two different things."Financial literacy means recognising both, rather than selecting investments solely because they promise higher returns.5. Do you understand how loans and credit cards work?Borrowing is not necessarily bad financial management. Home loans, education loans and business credit can serve important purposes.However, borrowers should understand interest rates, repayment schedules, processing fees, penalties and the total cost of borrowing.For example, a loan advertised at a relatively low monthly interest rate may be considerably more expensive when expressed as an annual rate.Similarly, paying only the minimum amount due on a credit card does not eliminate the remaining debt. Interest and other applicable charges can continue accumulating.Understanding these obligations helps prevent manageable borrowing from becoming a financial burden.6. Do you have an emergency fund and adequate insurance?Financial planning is not just about growing money. It is also about protecting yourself from unexpected expenses.An emergency fund helps cover essential expenses during job loss, medical emergencies or other financial disruptions. A commonly used starting point is three to six months of essential expenses, although the appropriate amount depends on income stability and family responsibilities.Insurance serves a different purpose. Health insurance can reduce the financial impact of medical expenses, while life insurance can provide financial protection to dependants.Understanding what a policy covers, its exclusions, premiums and claim conditions is as important as purchasing it.7. Do you understand how your income and investments are taxed?Knowing your salary is one thing. Understanding how much of it is taxable is another.CA Chandni Anandan, tax expert at ClearTax, said basic tax literacy means understanding taxable income, deductions, exemptions, tax deducted at source (TDS) and the differences between the old and new income tax regimes."Tax literacy does not mean knowing every section of the law. At a basic level, an individual should understand how their income is taxed, what makes up taxable income, which deductions or exemptions may apply to them, and how taxes already deducted through TDS affect their final liability."For investors, it also means knowing that short-term and long-term capital gains may be taxed differently, depending on the asset and applicable rules.Anandan further cautioned against assuming that tax deducted by an employer or bank settles the entire liability. Individuals should also review their Annual Information Statement (AIS), Form 26AS and income tax returns.Simply filing a return, even accurately, does not necessarily demonstrate an understanding of taxation.8. Can you recognise financial fraud and misleading investment advice?A message promising unusually high returns with little or no risk should raise questions, not excitement.Financial literacy involves recognising warning signs such as guaranteed returns, pressure to invest immediately, unsolicited stock tips and requests for sensitive banking information.It also means checking whether an investment intermediary is appropriately registered and understanding the product before transferring money.Here, Anooshka Soham Bathwal, CEO and founder of Dhanvesttor, warned that investors can be misled when they focus on a product's apparent benefits without assessing its suitability. She noted that people often follow recommendations from friends, agents or social media without understanding the associated risks, potential returns, costs or tax implications.“People may only pay attention to its benefits in terms of savings and ignore factors related to their suitability and needs,” she said, while shedding light on investors and their tendency to prioritise tax savings over overall financial well-being.Bathwal also highlighted the gender divide when it comes to financial decisions, observing that some women with substantial earnings still leave financial decisions to male relatives or consultants."Financial independence is not just about earning money; it’s also about having the knowledge and confidence to decide what to do with it."Her advice is to look beyond the promised benefit, understand the product and assess whether it fits one's financial goals and risk capacity before investing.9. Do you have a financial plan for the future?Financial goals change with age and circumstances. A first-time employee may prioritise an emergency fund, while someone approaching retirement may focus on income security.The important thing is to identify goals, estimate their costs and select appropriate saving or investment options.Retirement planning also requires understanding how inflation can increase future living expenses and how pension or retirement savings products work.Dr Shunil Tripathi, a financial literacy activist and trainer associated with financial education programmes of the RBI, Sebi, IRDAI and PFRDA,said a financially literate person connects savings and investments to specific goals and time frames rather than following market trends.The objective is not necessarily to maximise returns at every opportunity, but to make financial decisions that support long-term security.10. Can you make financial decisions independently?Perhaps the most important test of financial literacy is whether you can explain your financial choices.Do you understand why you hold a particular investment? Can you assess a loan offer without relying entirely on a salesperson? Would you question a financial recommendation that does not match your circumstances?Being financially literate does not mean never seeking professional advice. It means knowing enough to ask relevant questions and evaluate the answers.As financial programme trainer Dr Tripathi further said, "Someone who invests has taken an action. Someone who is financially literate understands why they took it.”It also means recognising that financial decisions should not be entirely outsourced to family members or advisers.The bigger pictureFinancial literacy does not mean knowing every investment scheme, tax provision or market mechanism. It means understanding the basics well enough to make informed decisions, recognise risks and ask the right questions.Also, the above 10 questions are not a formal test or a set of established rules to measure financial literacy. They are a starting point to help one reflect on their financial habits, identify gaps in understanding and take a more active interest in managing money.You do not have to become a financial expert overnight, nor does being financially literate mean managing everything on your own. The aim is to take an active interest in your finances, understand the decisions being made on your behalf and know when to seek professional advice. Experts can help you navigate complexity, but understanding your money remains your responsibility.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Roth IRA or 457(b): Which is better for your retirement savings? An expert weighs in
articles.summary: When deciding which savings vehicle to use, consider the tax advantages and penalties as well as the chance to get a matching contribution.
articles.body: Sometimes, the problem with savings is less about where to get the money than which savings vehicle to put them in, since they each have their own advantages and disadvantages. In this week’s Ask the Expert for CNN’s Savings Challenge, Douglas Boneparth, certified financial planner and founder of Bone Fide Wealth, breaks down the differences between a Roth IRA and a 457(b), which is offered to employees of some state and local governments and tax-exempt organizations. A reader from Florida asks: “I am skeptical of the future conditions of the economy and the status of Social Security. Where should I focus first for investing and saving for retirement? Roth or 457(b)? I often hear: do both, balance them out; but I am specifically asking which to maximize first. And if you have an explanation as to why, that would be very helpful.” DOUG: I love this question because you’re not asking whether to save for retirement. You already know you should. You’re asking how to do it smarter. That’s a much better conversation to be having. The 457(b) is an underrated account, especially for public employees. Unlike a 401(k), there’s no 10% early withdrawal penalty, meaning you can tap it before age 59½ without penalty. If early retirement is part of the plan, that matters a lot. Contributions also reduce your taxable income today, which is valuable if you’re in a higher bracket now. However, the Roth is powered by something the 457(b) can’t match: tax-free growth and tax-free withdrawals in retirement. You pay taxes now and you never pay taxes on that money again. And here’s where your Social Security concern gets interesting. Roth withdrawals don’t count toward the income thresholds that determine how much of your benefit gets taxed. If benefits shrink or get taxed more aggressively down the road (which is a legitimate concern) having a tax-free income source gives you flexibility a pre-tax account simply can’t. If your 457(b) has an employer match, grab it first. But if you’re forced to prioritize one, go with the Roth. Tax-free income in retirement is one of the most powerful tools available to today’s savers. And given your skepticism about Social Security, you might sleep better at night knowing you had that tax-free bucket to draw from. Have your own savings question for Doug? Please send it to savingschallenge@cnn.com. Tip of the week: Even if you can only save a little, compounding can help … a lot Consistently saving and investing even small amounts of money can grow into an impressive nest egg over time. For example, if you consistently save $200 a month ($2,400 a year) from ages 25 to 65 in a pre-tax account like a 401(k), 403(b) or deductible IRA, you could have a $512,000 nest egg by age 65, according to the Plan Sponsor Council of America. That assumes an average annual return of 7%. If you can only salt away $100 a month ($1,200 a year pre-tax), but your employer offers a dollar-for-dollar match on that amount, you still can end up with half a million dollars after 40 years. And if you’re able to save $200 after-tax in a Roth IRA, you will have half a million dollars tax-free when you retire.

Douglas Boneparth, a certified financial planner, is founder of Bone Fide Wealth and coauthor of "Money Together," a book about couples and finances.

articles.title: HDFC Bank deputy MD Kaizad Bharucha announces decision to quit ahead of Anup Bagchi's takeover as CEO
articles.summary: HDFC Bank Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha has resigned from the country's largest private sector lender, with his exit scheduled for December 31,
articles.body: HDFC Bank Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha has resigned from the country's largest private sector lender, with his exit scheduled for December 31, the bank said in an exchange filing on Saturday.Bharucha, who joined the bank in 1995, had requested cessation from service with effect from December 31, reported PTI. The bank's board has accepted his request and decided to forward it to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for approval.The development comes days before Anup Bagchi, a veteran of the ICICI Group, takes over as HDFC Bank's Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer on October 27. Bharucha was reportedly among those in contention for elevation to the top post.The announcement comes as HDFC Bank reported a rise in profitability for the July-September quarter. Its consolidated net profit increased 5.55 per cent year-on-year to Rs 20,700 crore, compared with Rs 19,611 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.On a standalone basis, net profit grew 4.7 per cent to Rs 19,510 crore. Total income rose to Rs 97,258 crore from Rs 91,040 crore a year earlier, while total expenditure increased to Rs 67,774 crore from Rs 63,117 crore.The bank's provisions and contingencies edged up to Rs 3,573.62 crore from Rs 3,500 crore in the year-ago quarter. HDFC Bank said profit after tax, excluding treasury performance, grew 12.6 per cent year-on-year.Asset quality improved during the quarter, with the gross non-performing assets (GNPA) ratio declining to 1.11 per cent as of September 30, from 1.17 per cent in the preceding quarter and 1.24 per cent a year earlier.The bank's overall capital adequacy ratio stood at 18.9 per cent at the end of September, compared with 20 per cent a year ago.You use AI every day. articles.title: Wall Street's record breakouts unravel as investors dump recent winners: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: The S&P 500's record breakout has reversed, yet most of its stocks still finished the week higher.
articles.body:
The S&P 500's record breakout has reversed. Most of its stocks still finished the week higher.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) lost roughly 2% this week, with selling accelerating into Friday. It finished near 7,659, back below the August high it finally cleared earlier this month.

New records were supposed to open the door to another advance. Buyers couldn't keep it open.

The index reached nearly 7,845 on Oct. 6, briefly exceeding its August peak near 7,817. Friday's close left that breakout underwater.

That's the setup for a bull trap — a move above an established high that reverses, catching investors who bought the breakout.

The pattern is repeating across some of the market's biggest names.

The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) lost roughly 4.5% this week, reversing its recent breakout above earlier summer and September highs.

The Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund ( XLK ) and Nvidia ( NVDA ) also broke above records set months earlier. Both have since fallen back below those peaks.

Palantir ( PLTR ) took nearly a year to reclaim its November record. Its brief victory quickly unraveled , and Friday's close confirmed a correction — leaving the stock down roughly 11% for the week.

The selling is landing hardest on many of the stocks investors had rewarded most.

Eighteen of the S&P's 20 biggest weekly decliners ranked among its 100 strongest performers from March 30 through Oct. 6, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

Dell ( DELL ) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise ( HPE ) both more than tripled during that earlier advance. Both lost over 20% this week.

Yet buyers haven't abandoned the market.

Roughly 72% of S&P constituents finished the week higher. The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF ( RSP ) gained roughly 0.5%. By giving each company roughly the same weight, it reduces the influence of the biggest stocks — showing how their losses can obscure gains elsewhere.

The reversal in leadership is striking. The 100 strongest S&P stocks from March 30 through Oct. 6 lost roughly 5% on average this week. The 100 weakest gained roughly 4%.

The immediate repair job is reclaiming roughly 7,800 on the S&P and 27,200–27,300 on the Nasdaq — then holding those levels.

Buying beyond the former leaders is giving the market some support. If that participation holds, it could help the indexes recover. If it fades, the failed breakouts would become a broader warning.

articles.title: Why oil prices could be poised for a 'super spike': Analyst
articles.summary: Crude oil is near $95 a barrel, and William Blair energy research analyst Neal Dingmann thinks the next move could be a "super spike."
articles.body:
Crude oil ( CL=F ) is trading near $100 a barrel, Brent ( BZ=F ) is around $110, and William Blair energy research analyst Neal Dingmann thinks the next move could be a "super spike."

"We could see a super spike like a lot of the CEOs of the majors have suggested," Dingmann told Yahoo Finance Senior Reporter Brooke DiPalma (video above). "Do I think that's possible? Absolutely."

Dingmann noted that oil executives keep telling him prices have a new, higher floor for at least the next several quarters, and he agrees: The midcycle price most analysts used to put at $70 to $80 a barrel is now "probably closer to 80 to 90," with periods above $100.

"You've had Iranian tanker attacks, you've had record freight cost," Dingmann explained. "It's really the underlying physical market that continues to get tighter and tighter."

The energy sector ( XLE ) is up more than 50% this year — the best of the S&P 500's ( ^GSPC ) 11 sectors and well ahead of the index's roughly 12% gain. US crude has climbed more than 70% since Dec. 31, and Brent, the global benchmark, is up about 80%.

Dingmann added that geopolitical and political events "have now caused actual physical events," and stopgaps will be hard to pull off: "It's going to be very difficult to try to release barrels from the SPR or other temporary fixes."

The Strategic Petroleum Reserve has already fallen to its lowest level since 1982.

And then there's diesel: Heating oil futures ( HO=F ), a benchmark for diesel, have more than doubled this year.

"I think we've already seen record highs and we're going to even see higher," Dingmann said, pointing to "diesel, gasoline, home heating fuels" as winter approaches.

That's bad news for consumers and good news for US oil producers, which Dingmann said "are just going to continue to print money." Most of the companies he covers reported record free cash flow in the second quarter, he said, and he expects new records in the third or fourth quarter.

Not everyone on Wall Street thinks oil is about to spike. Goldman Sachs on Monday raised its December target for Brent to $90 a barrel and $81 for US crude, both below where oil trades now. The bank sees Brent reaching $125 only if oil infrastructure is damaged, shipping attacks intensify, or the risk premium persists.

articles.title: House-help app Snabbit burns Rs 195 crore to chase Rs 12-crore revenues in FY26
articles.summary: Instant househelp startup Snabbit, which has raised $112 million in venture capital money, earned Rs 12.2 crore in operating revenue for fiscal year 2026
articles.body: Instant househelp startup Snabbit, which has raised $112 million in venture capital money, earned Rs 12.2 crore in operating revenue for fiscal year 2026 while incurring a Rs 168 crore loss, according to financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies. The numbers reflect the fast growing and high-cash-burn nature of the 10-minute househelp space, in which Snabbit competes against Urban Company and General Catalyst-backed startup Pronto.Snabbit, backed by the likes of Nexus Venture Partners and Lightspeed, started operations in August 2024, making FY26 its first full year of operations.The Bengaluru-based company’s total expenses stood at Rs 195 crore during the year. Expert service costs (paid to its professionals) of Rs 63.1 crore were its biggest expense for the year, followed by marketing costs at Rs 48.7 crore, employee benefit expenses of Rs 46 crore and others.The operating revenue included Rs 1.4 crore from sale of uniforms to its professionals. Snabbit also reported Rs 14.8 crore in interest income, taking its total revenue to Rs 27 crore in FY26.Operationally, Snabbit reported an earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) loss of Rs 181.5 crore in FY26."Given the pace of growth and the investments required to build this category from the ground up, FY26 financials do not fully reflect the underlying economics or the maturity of the business today," Snabbit founder and CEO Aayush Aggarwal said in a statement. "As we continue to scale, the benefits of operating leverage, improving unit economics and increasing network density are becoming increasingly evident."Founded by Aayush Agarwal, Snabbit offers hyperlocal, on-demand home services such as general cleaning, dishwashing, and laundry in 10 minutes. It has recently expanded to at-home beauty services through Blush.In January, amid fierce competition, Accel-backed househelp startup Pync shut down with its founders joining Snabbit in senior roles across operations and business.ET has been reporting on the sector’s increasing spend over the last few months. Cash burn across the instant househelp sector rose 14% month on month (MoM) to $16-17 million in June. In May, the combined cash burn of Urban Company’s InstaHelp, Snabbit, and Pronto stood at $14-15 million.The startups have been raising funding to sustain their rapid growth. The board of listed home services platform Urban Company will meet on October 16 to consider a fresh fundraise, according to an exchange filing by the company on Tuesday. Urban Company is planning to raise Rs 2,000-2,500 crore via a qualified institutional placement (QIP), per sources.In April, Snabbit raised $56 million (around Rs 529 crore) in a round co-led by Susquehanna Venture Capital, Unicorn Growth Fund and Bertelsmann India Investments. The round valued the startup at $350 million, almost double its $180 million valuation in October.Rival Pronto also closed a $45 million round in May this year from US-based technology investor Lachy Groom, Epiq Capital, General Catalyst, and Bain Capital Ventures. The startup’s post-money valuation was $200 million.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
